 JUDGMENT

The petitioners have filed this petition U/Sec 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, claiming compensation of Rs.40,00,000/ for the death of Sri.Santhosh.N.C, in the road traffic accident occurred on 16.02.2022.
02.

The brief facts are as under: It is submitted that on 16.02.2022 at about 09.45 p.m one Santhosh.N.C was riding the twowheeler bearing No.TN70W0839 from Hosur to Avalapalli,
near Sarojamma Building, Bharathiyar Nagar, with due care and caution, at that time the driver of Bolero Pickup LGV No.KA51C1325 came from Hosur to Avalapalli Road with high speed, in rash and negligent manner, without giving any signal, suddenly stopped the vehicle on the middle of the road.
Due to this the rider of Motor Cycle dashed against the Bolero vehicle at its back.
Due to this the rider i.e., Santhosh.N.C fell down and sustained grievous injuries and died on the spot itself.
Immediately the dead body was shifted to (SCCH3) 4 M.V.C.No.1138/2022 Hosur Government hospital wherein post mortem was conducted and the dead body was handed over to the petitioners.

Thereafter the petitioners have performed last rites and rituals by spending Rs.2,00,000/
including funeral, transportation etc.,.
That the deceased prior to the accident was hale and healthy and was working as Helper under private owner Srinivasan and earning Rs.30,000/ per month.
The deceased was the only bread earner in the family.
Due to the death of deceased the petitioners being the wife, children, mother and sister have lost their love and affection and great financial loss.
The accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of Bolero vehicle driver.
Even a criminal case was registered against said Bolero vehicle driver.
The respondent No.1 is the insurer and the respondent No.2 is the owner of the said Bolero vehicle.

Hence both respondents are jointly and Swetha.N vs Icici Lomb Gen Ins Co Ltd on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/90903084/
2 severally liable to pay the compensation.

sentences.text: Hence this petition.
03. After service of notice, the respondent No.2 did not appeared before this court on the date fixed for his appearance and hence he was placed absent throughout the proceedings of the petition.
However the respondent No.1 have appeared before this Court through their counsel and filed written statement.

(SCCH3) 5 M.V.C.No.1138/2022 04. The averments of the written statement of respondent No.1 is as under: This respondent has denied issuance of policy in respect of vehicle bearing No.KA51C1325 in favour of respondent No.2.
The respondent No.2 has not informed about the accident.
The petition is bad for nonjoinder of necessary parties.
The Bolero vehicle driver was not holding valid driving licence on the date of accident.
The death is due to the sole negligence of the deceased only.
This respondent has denied manner of accident, age, avocation, income and expenses incurred by the petitioners for the deceased.
There is no fitness certificate and Permit to the offending Bolero vehicle as on the date of accident and the respondent No.2 has violated terms and conditions of the policy.
Hence this respondent is not liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
The claim of the petitioners is too excessive and exorbitant and hence prays to dismiss the petition with costs.
05. In order to prove the case, the petitioner No.1 was got examined herself as PW.1 and got marked 23 documents as Ex.P.1 to 23 and closed their side.

(SCCH3) 6 M.V.C.No.1138/2022 06. By way of rebuttal, the Manager of the respondent No.1 got examined herself as RW.1 and closed their side.
07.
Heard arguments from both sides.
08. Based on the aforesaid pleadings, the following issues have been framed:  ISSUES 01.
Whether petitioners prove that they are the LRs/dependants of deceased Sri.Santhosh.N.C S/o late Chandrashekar?

02. Whether petitioners prove that deceased Sri.Santhosh.N.C S/o late Chandrashekar died in RTA arising out of the accident alleged to have been taken place on 16.02.2022 at about 09.45 p.m, near Sarojamma building, Avalapalli Road, Bharathiyar Nagar, due to negligent act of driving of the Bolero Pickup LGV vehicle bearing registration No. KA51C 1325 by its driver as alleged in the petition?
03. Whether petitioners are entitled for compensation?
If so, what amount & from whom?
04 . What order or award?

sentences.text: 09. My findings on the aforesaid issues are as under: (SCCH3) 7 M.V.C.No.1138/2022 Issue No.1 In affirmative Issue No.2 In affirmative Issue No.3 In partly affirmative Issue No.4

As per final order for the following:
REASONS 10. Issues No.1 and 2:
These issues will be taken at one stretch for my consideration in order to avoid repetition of facts as they are interrelated with each other.

It is the grievance of the petitioners that the deceased Sri.Santhosh.N.C died in road traffic accident which took place on 16.02.2022 due to the rash and negligent driving of offending Bolero LGV vehicle driver.
Further they have contended that they are the legal heirs and dependents of deceased.
Due to the death of deceased, the petitioners have lost love and affection and facing hardship.

Hence, they have claimed compensation of Rs.40,00,000/.
11.

Per contra, the same was denied by respondent No.1 and stated that the accident did not took place due to the negligence of the Bolero vehicle driver but it is due to the negligence of the deceased (SCCH3) 8 M.V.C.No.1138/2022 himself.
Hence they are not liable to pay the compensation.
12. In order to prove this, the petitioner No.1 was got examined herself as PW.1 by reiterating all the averments of the petition in her affidavit.
The PW.1 in her crossexamination admitted that "That in my home we are four persons i.e., myself, my child, motherin law and sisterinlaw.
That sister inlaw is aged about 29 years and unmarried.
It is true that I am residing at Nelamangala Bengaluru.
That the employer of my husband had lodged the complaint to the Police.
It is true that I had lodged the complaint to the Police.
That my husband was working as helper but I do not know where he was working.
That as per information given by my husband he told that he was working under one Srinivas on Rs.1,000/ per day.
That my husband was working as helper since 5 months back from the date of accident.
That my husband was proceeding daily from Nelamangala to Hosuru through Bus.
I do not know what kind of work the said Srinivas was doing.
I do not know to whom the motor cycle bearing No. TN70W0839 belongs to in which my husband was proceeding.
That my husband was having Driving license.
I can produce the said Driving license.
I do not (SCCH3) 9 M.V.C.No.1138/2022 know from which Insurance Company the motor cycle bearing No TN70W 0839 was insured.
That the police have informed me about the accident.
The police came to my home and informed me about the accident.
It is true that I have not produced any documents to show avocation and income of my husband.
That my sister inlaw is not working anywhere.
That now we are Tailoring work for our livelihood".
Further the PW.1 had denied all other suggestions of the respondent No.1 counsel.
The PW.1 had not seen the accident and she had deposed based on the available documents on record.
13. Per contra, the Manager of the respondent No.1 was got examined herself as RW.1 by reiterating all the averments of the written statement in her affidavit.
Further in her cross examination the RW.1 has admitted that "I do not know that the offending driver and owner have not challenged the charge sheet.
It is true that in the charge sheet it is stated that when the vehicle was proceeding it has applied sudden brake, but it is wrong.

We have not produced any document to show that the Swetha.N vs Icici Lomb Gen Ins Co Ltd on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/90903084/
4 offending driver had no Driving licence, FC and permit.

sentences.text: It is true that the deceased in this case is third party".
(SCCH3) 10 M.V.C.No.1138/2022 14. The PW.1 in support of her case has got marked entire police documents as per Ex.P.1 to 5, 22 and 23.

On perusal of these documents, it is clear that the concerned I.O after investigation have filed Charge sheet against the Bolero LGV vehicle driver bearing No.KA51C1325 for the alleged offences punishable U/s 279, 304(A) of IPC.
Further as per Ex.P.23 the concerned I.O has stated that the deceased died only due to the rash and negligent driving of offending Bolero LGV vehicle driver.
15. It is pertinent to note that the PW.1 had marked the Mahazar, Sketch and IMV report as per Ex.P.2, 3 and 22 which supports the version of the petitioners.

Eventhough the respondent No.1 contend that the petition is bad for nonjoinder of necessary parties and the accident was not caused by the offending Bolero LGV vehicle driver, but to prove this except examining its Manager,
they have not adduced any rebuttal evidence or not produced any supportive documents.
16. Further the respondent No.1 has contended that the deceased was not wearing helmet at the time of accident.
It is true that the police records is silent in this regard.
Further the respondent No.1 have not (SCCH3) 11 M.V.C.No.1138/2022 proved that non wearing of helmet is a cause for accident and death.

17. The counsel for petitioners has relied upon the decision reported in a. 2023 ACJ 1234 - Manager,
National Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s Amruta and others - It is observed that non wearing of helmet may not attributed to contributory negligence of the deceased for the accident.

a. 2023 ACJ 1234 - Manager,
National Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s Amruta and others

sentences.text: 18. Even the respondent No.1 is relying upon the police records and from the police records also the alleged contributory negligence of the deceased cannot be considered.
It is true that the PW.1 in her cross examination has given contradictory version but from this her entire oral evidence and the document cannot be discarded.

Hence with the available documents and in absence of supportive documents by the respondents, I am of opinion that the petitioners are successful in proving that the deceased died due to the accidental injuries only caused by the offending Bolero LGV vehicle driver.

19. Further the petitioners in order to prove that they are the legal heirs and dependents of the deceased have produced Notarized copy of Death certificate of deceased and his father, Aadhaar cards (SCCH3) 12 M.V.C.No.1138/2022 and Elections ID cards of themselves and deceased, SSLC,
PUC markscard, PAN card of deceased, Birth certificate of petitioner No.2 and Marriage certificate as per Ex.P.6 to 21.
It is true that petitioner No.4 is the sister of the deceased who was unmarried.
Hence she can be considered as dependent on the deceased.

So, on basis of these documents, I am of opinion that the petitioners No.1 to 4 are the wife, daughter, mother and sister of the deceased who can be considered as dependents and legal heirs of deceased.
Hence, I answered issue No.1 in affirmative and issue No.2 in affirmative.

sentences.text: Issue No.3:

As per above findings, it is clear that the accident took place due to negligent driving of the offending Bolero vehicle driver and the husband of the petitioner No.1 died on the spot due to fatal injuries.

Hence the petitioners No.1 to 4 being the dependents of deceased are entitled for compensation as under:
a) Loss of dependency:-
The petitioners submitted that the deceased was aged about 31 years as on the date of accident.

To prove the same, they have produced Aadhaar card, Election ID card, Driving licence, SSLC, PUC marks card and PAN card of the (SCCH3) 13 M.V.C.No.1138/2022 deceased as per Ex.P.7 to 12 which shows that the deceased was born on 14.07.1991.
According to it the age of the deceased as on the date of accident would be 32 years and the same is considered for calculating the compensation.
So, as per Sarla Varma and others Vs Delhi Transport Corporation and others case reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 the multiplier applicable is "16" and the same is considered.

entities.text: Sarla Varma and others Vs Delhi Transport Corporation and others case reported in 2009 ACJ 1298
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In order to prove the income of the deceased, the petitioners have not produced any documents or not adduced any evidence.

Hence under these circumstances it is just and proper to consider notional income fixed as per Minimum Wages Act by considering the deceased as an unskilled worker which comes to Rs.13,311/ per month.

Since the deceased has left four dependents, as per Sarla Varma and others Vs Delhi Transport Corporation and others case reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 if the dependents are 4 to 6, then personal deduction is to be 1/4th.

entities.text: Sarla Varma and others Vs Delhi Transport Corporation and others case reported in 2009 ACJ 1298
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence, in this case 1/4th deduction has to be done towards personal expenses.

So, after deduction of 1/4th (Rs.3,327/), then the income comes to Rs.9,984/.
(SCCH3) 14 M.V.C.No.1138/2022
As above stated that apart from the deceased there are no one to look after the petitioners.
As per Judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in Sarla Varma and others Vs Delhi Transport Corporation and others case reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 the petitioners are entitled for future prospects.

entities.text: Sarla Varma and others Vs Delhi Transport Corporation and others case reported in 2009 ACJ 1298
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The deceased being self employed and aged below 40 years, then 40% of the income (Rs.3,993/) to be added towards future prospects, then the income for calculation comes to Rs.13,977/.

Hence the petitioners are entitled for Rs.13,977 x 12 x 16 =
Rs.26,83,584/ under this head.
b) Loss of estate and funeral expenses:

Since it is settled law in National Insurance Company Ltd.,
Vs Pranay Sethi and others case in AIR 2017 SC 5157
that the dependents would be entitled for loss of estate to the extent of Rs.15,000/ and funeral expenses to the extent of Rs.15,000/, as such I award the same.
c) Loss of consortium:

In this case the petitioner No.1 being the widow of the deceased is entitled for Rs.40,000/ towards spousal consortium, the petitioner No.2 being the minor daughter of the (SCCH3) 15 M.V.C.No.1138/2022 deceased is entitled for Rs.40,000/ towards parental consortium and petitioner No.3 being the mother of the deceased is entitled for Rs.40,000/
towards filial consortium.

But the petitioner No.4 being the unmarried sister of the deceased is not entitled for any amount under this head as per Judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court in United India Insurance Co. Ltd., Vs Satinder Kaur @ Satwinder Kaur & Ors case and Magma General Insurance Company case in (2018) 18 SCC 130.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Magma General Insurance Company case in (2018) 18 SCC 130
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence I award the same.

sentences.text: Thus the petitioners are entitled for compensation under the following heads:

1.Loss of dependency Rs.26,83,584/
2.Loss of estate 15,000/
3.Towards spousal consortium (for 40,000/ petitioner No.1)
4.Towards parental consortium (for 40,000/ petitioner No.2)
5.Towards filial consortium (for 40,000/ petitioner No.3)
6.Transportation of dead body and 15,000/ funeral expenses Total Rs.28,33,584/ (SCCH3) 16 M.V.C.No.1138/2022 22.
Regarding liability: The petitioners have proved that deceased had sustained injuries due to rash and negligent driving of offending Car driver.

The respondent No.1 has denied issuance of policy to the offending vehicle in its written statement, but later examined its Manager as RW.1 who admits issuance of policy to the offending Bolero vehicle and its validity in its affidavit evidence.
Hence the said Bolero vehicle is owned by the respondent No.2 and insured with the respondent No.1.
Hence, the respondents No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.

23. With regard to apportionment is concerned, petitioner No.1 being the wife of the deceased is entitled for 50% and petitioners No.2 and 3 being the minor daughter and mother of the deceased are entitled for 20% each and petitioner No.4 being the sister of the deceased is entitled for 10% of the amount awarded.
Hence, the issue No.3 is answered in partly affirmative.
24. Issue No.3:

In view of my findings on issues No.1 to 3 as above and with regard to awarding (SCCH3) 17 M.V.C.No.1138/2022 the interest is concerned, the petitioners are entitled for simple interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till deposit.
As such I proceed to pass the following: ORDER
The claim petition filed by the petitioners U/Sec 166 of the M.V. Act is hereby allowed in part, with costs.

The petitioners are entitled for Rs.28,33,584/ (Twenty eight lakhs thirty three thousand five hundred and eighty four only) as compensation with interest at 6% p.a from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
The respondents No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation amount to the petitioners.

However, in view of valid insurance policy, respondent No.1  Insurance Company is directed to pay the awarded compensation amount and shall deposit the same within time stipulated under section 168(3) of M.V. Act.

sentences.text: On deposit of the compensation amount with interest, petitioner No.1 is entitled for 50%, petitioner (SCCH3) 18 M.V.C.No.1138/2022 No.2 and 3 are entitled for 20% each and petitioner No.4 is entitled for 10% of compensation as awarded.

Out of the share amount of petitioner No.1 along with interest accrued, 40% of the amount shall be deposited in her name in any nationalized or schedule bank for a period of three years and the remaining 60% of the amount shall be released to her through Epayment on proper identification without any further proceedings.
However, petitioner No.1 is at liberty to withdraw the periodical interest accrued on her deposit amount from time to time.

Out of the share amount of petitioner No.2 along with interest accrued, entire amount shall be deposited in her name in any nationalized or schedule bank till she attain the age of majority, on proper identification.
However, the petitioner No.1 is at liberty to withdraw the periodical interest accrued on her deposit amount from time to time and to use the same for the benefit of the minor petitioner No.2.
Out of the share amount of petitioners No.3 and 4 along with interest accrued, entire amount shall be released to them through Epayment on proper identification without any further proceedings.

The advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/.

To prove the same, they have produced Aadhaar card, Election ID card, Driving licence, SSLC, PUC marks card and PAN card of the (SCCH3) 13 M.V.C.No.1138/2022 deceased as per Ex.P.7 to 12 which shows that the deceased was born on 14.07.1991.
According to it the age of the deceased as on the date of accident would be 32 years and the same is considered for calculating the compensation.
In order to prove the income of the deceased, the petitioners have not produced any documents or not adduced any evidence.
Hence under these circumstances it is just and proper to consider notional income fixed as per Minimum Wages Act by considering the deceased as an unskilled worker which comes to Rs.13,311/ per month.
Since the deceased has left four dependents, as per Sarla Varma and others Vs Delhi Transport Corporation and others case reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 if the dependents are 4 to 6, then personal deduction is to be 1/4th.
Hence, in this case 1/4th deduction has to be done towards personal expenses.
So, after deduction of 1/4th (Rs.3,327/), then the income comes to Rs.9,984/.

The deceased being self employed and aged below 40 years, then 40% of the income (Rs.3,993/) to be added towards future prospects, then the income for calculation comes to Rs.13,977/.
